comments.text: Load 31: low bytes of the handler addresses for entity types $00–$2F. Pair each byte with the byte at the same index in $7F0F–$7F3E: $2027 reads this byte with Y = the entity's type from $1919,X and $202A stores it in the low byte of the JSR at $2036, which runs with A = $1A29,X. Only positive types reach the table: $1FE1 skips an empty slot (type 0) and $2024 sends a negative type (a pickup) to $203C, so entry $00 is never called. Load 31: little-endian update target $91A1. The resident indirect jump at $0450, the last step of a main-loop pass, takes it while the game-exit flag $0840 is zero, the selected player's meter $4DCD,X is nonzero and the status $5284 that $7B84 returns is nonzero. The eight-page character copy from $7F41, which starts at $8E71, also takes the routine's bytes from $D330 on, as characters $66–$67; none of the load's four metatile corner tables names them, so the map never draws them.
A little-endian pointer to the eight-page source copied to RAM beneath I/O by $34DD and $717C.

Load 31: values $00, $0C, $06. $6C62–$6C70 copies them to $529C and $529D, the shadows of the shared multicolour registers $D022 and $D023, and to $6F, which the split interrupt writes to the background register $D021 at $133F. $33C1–$33CA copies the first two to $529C and $529D again when $3384 restores the display after a stage-object interaction. Load 31: player frame byte $66. $6C4A stores it at $4A and stores the value minus $66 modulo 256 at $1177.

Load 31: the player's starting X low, X high and Y bytes, $0E, $01 and $A2. $6C31–$6C3E copies them to $47–$49. At stage start $03B8–$03C4 also tests the X bytes: when X high is zero and X low is below $AB, $03C6 sets $4D6A to 7, otherwise to 0.

Load 31: the map's row stride in bytes, $80. The scroll routines add it to the map source pointer at $2D35 and $2D62 (scrolling right) and $2E2A and $2E57 (left), and $4738 uses it as the offset of the lower pair when $471B writes a stage record's two-by-two block of metatiles.

Load 31: the map's width in metatiles, $40. The rightward-scroll check at $0EF7–$0F02 compares the metatile column just past the view's right edge with it and skips the scroll when that column is not smaller, and the entity rightward move at $4593 undoes a move whose next column equals it.
The downward-scroll check at $0CCC–$0CD9 compares the next map-row position with this value.

Load 31: the view origin, column $59 and row $0A in characters. The screen builder $6D17 halves them at $6D26 and $6D2B to find the first metatile to draw; $6D8B–$6DA0 copies them to the left and top view bounds and computes right and bottom by adding $25 and $12 modulo 256; $6DA3–$6DBE scrolls once more down or right for an odd row or column; and $6DC1–$6DD6 stores the final bounds, adding $26 and $13. $33EC–$3408 saves both bytes, puts the current view's left and top ($569B, $569D) there for $6D17 to redraw the screen, and restores them.
The little-endian address $9AB7 of this load’s entity records. $1863 copies it into the pointer at $E2–$E3.

The initial entity-slot limit is 1. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 1 ($18CB). The load has 1 entity records, all of which the initializer loads, stopping at the zero byte after them; each pass, the slot scan at $3622 checks slots 1 to 1 ($3629), and since no record follows, $3632 finds that zero byte and reloads an empty slot's own record at $366A.

Load 31: bytes $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, $00, the base frames of six reward pickups. $49E3 picks a random start and scans the eight bytes $7F5E–$7F65 at $49E9 for a nonzero one, so a zero byte disables its entry; the last two of the eight are $7F64/$7F65. Entries 0–5 jump through the table at $4A02/$4A0A to $5F88, $5F90, $5FA0, $5FA8, $5F98 and $5FB0, which load the entry’s byte into Y and the reward $05, $10, $20, $50, $10 or $00 into A; $5FB5 patches Y into the LDA at $5FC5, which stores it as the type-$FA entity’s frame $19E5/$19C3, and stores A in $1AB1,X, which the contact handler $7656 passes to $7756. In load 31 all eight bytes $7F5E–$7F65 are zero, so the scan at $49E9 would never end if $49E3 ran.

A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and ($5A) at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code to one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

Load 31: the first 16 low bytes of the split map-row pointer table at $85CF; the matching high bytes begin at $8620. These entries point to $8671 through $8DF1 in 128-byte steps. The drawing path reads the pair at $6D30–$6D39. The remaining entries are described separately.

Load 31: low bytes for pointer entries 16–79 of the 81-entry split table. Paired with the high table, these encode $8E71 through $ADF1 in 128-byte steps modulo 65536, the row stride at $7F4A. They lie beyond the map’s 16 rows, the count at $7F4C. The window draw at $6D30 and the scroll readers at $2CD4, $2DC9, $2EC2 and $2F9D index by the view’s rows, which the scroll check at $0CCC keeps within the map. The hero’s tile checks index the table by his row $6F3D ($0EA7, $1041, $6E77) or that row plus one ($0C47, $0C69, $6E8D); $6F3D reaches 16 when the view is at the bottom of the map and the hero at his lowest screen position $E1 ($0CFC), so entries 16 and 17 can be read, and no hero check reaches entries 18–79. The entity collision checks at $451D and $4638 index the table by an entity’s tile row from $71DB, plus one to three, with no bound of their own.
